[Source page 1]

                 KREATIV WORKSHOP

   FIND YOUR VOICE WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

               The Synthetic Party by Computer Lars

Workshop description
Facilitated by Computer Lars from The Synthetic Party  school students will experiment with
artificial intelligence to thematize the upcoming parliamentary election. Students will have to find their
own voice through practical exercises on how artificial intelligence expresses itself through
data created by humans. The result is that each student creates one image and one text that
can illustrate a political issue relevant to them.

Each student brings a computer (possibly sharing in groups of 2), and links to tools are sent
out in advance. These are the first workshops of their kind, but could eventually become a general
offering. Therefore, the organizer, Asker Bryld Staunæs, wishes to evaluate with both teachers
and students to determine how it becomes interesting for young people to create with artificial
intelligence, so the format can be targeted precisely at those who will gain voting rights in a few years.

[Source page 2]

Background

              Excerpt from "design series for a new Christiansborg" by The Synthetic Party

Our knowledge of young people's democratic and digital education has been challenged in a time when
algorithms exercise control over content on social media, and one cannot know whether
the internet's images and texts were made by a human or a machine. A long
series of new didactic and educational challenges arise now that artificial intelligence itself can
write a whole article and create new photorealistic images through a simple text description.

Art can offer a unique method to understand the discreet power of the digital public sphere.
Therefore, the artist group Computer Lars together with the tech hub MindFuture offers two
workshops over the fall2022 about The Synthetic Party - a platform for democracy and
artificial intelligence. The workshops will consist of a performative lecture by Computer Lars,
followed by hands-on exercises for students  in using image and text generation as a
method to explore digital culture. Finally, the students will “generate” their own politics
- as an illustrated principle program - on a topic related to the upcoming election.

The workshops introduce graduating and high school students  to easy tools  to create
with artificial intelligence. One could say that artificial intelligence today has learned its abilities by
reading the entire cultural archive, which contains all the images and texts that ordinary
people have put on the internet. By understanding how to communicate with the machine
through text descriptions - so-called prompts  -, the students can gain insight  into the algorithms'
hidden basis through a play with its “mash-up” of the common human expression.

[Source page 3]
